title: 1997 AHSME Problem 13
statement: How many two-digit positive integers \(N\) have the property that the sum of \(N\) and the number obtained by reversing the order of the digits of \(N\) is a perfect square?

solutions.text: The sum is \(11(x+y).\) Since \(1\le x+y\le18,\) this is square only when \(x+y=11,\) giving \(121.\) The tens digit \(x\) can be any of \(2,3,\ldots,9,\) with \(y=11-x.\) There are \(8\) integers, so E is correct.
hints: Determine when \(11(x+y)\), with \(1\le x\le9\) and \(0\le y\le9\), can be square
